## What happened

`release:checkpoint-run` (a singleton write a caller must not blindly retry) returned a
bounded/trimmed reply whose visible body was just `{ summary: '[payload preview omitted...]',
_projection: {...} }` — no `ok`, `launched`, `candidate`, or `unit`. The caller could not tell
whether the gate suite had actually launched (EI-21058972492075433).

## Root cause (non-obvious)

`projectBoundedPayload` (`libs/generic/tooldef/src/payload-tier.ts`) walks the response data
with a budget of `target - 1_600` chars (`target` = 7,000 for `trimmed`, 18,000 for `standard`),
reserving a flat 1,600 chars for the `_projection` metadata it builds AFTER the walk (the
omission-sample list, the recovery `cursor.args`, the `next` prose). The walk itself correctly
*prioritizes* identity-shaped fields (`ok`, `id`, ...) so they survive even when other fields get
trimmed.

But the 1,600-char metadata reserve is a flat constant, while the metadata it has to cover scales
with how MUCH got trimmed:

- up to `GENERIC_PROJECTION_OMISSION_SAMPLES` (20) omission entries, each `{path, reason}` — for a
  rich, deeply-nested receipt (a repair-queue object, several arrays, a long prose note) these
  fill up fast and can alone exceed 1,600 chars;
- `cursor.args`, independently bounded up to `GENERIC_PROJECTION_CURSOR_ARGS_TARGET_CHARS` (2,000);
- the recovery `next` string (a few hundred chars).

So a payload that is genuinely COMPLEX enough to need heavy trimming (exactly the case where the
walk correctly preserved `ok`/`launched`/`candidate` at the expense of everything else) is also
the case where its OWN bookkeeping about what got trimmed is largest — and that bookkeeping,
added on top of the already-in-budget preview, could push the final size over `target`.

The "exact last-line defense" then fired: `metadata.returnedChars >= target` → replace the WHOLE
`result` with a bare `{ summary: '[payload preview omitted...]' }`. This discarded the identity
fields that HAD fit, purely because of metadata the walk itself generated describing everything
else that didn't.

## The fix

In that fallback branch, build a SEPARATE, small, independently-budgeted identity-only preview
(reusing the existing `projectIdentityPreview` helper, the same one the depth-limit boundary
already uses) and merge it with the metadata, instead of discarding data entirely. Only when
nothing identifiable survives even that (no `id`/`ok`/`launched`/... anywhere) does it fall back
to the bare summary — there's genuinely nothing left to preserve at that point.

Also added `launched`, `candidate`, `unit`, `runId` to the shared `IDENTITY_FIELDS` set
(previously just `id`/`title`/`ok`/`status`/... generic CRUD-style names) — write/launch tool
receipts carry a DIFFERENT outcome-identity shape than a get/list tool, and deserve the same
prioritization `ok` already got.

## Why this generalizes

This is a framework-level defect in `libs/generic/tooldef`, not specific to
`release:checkpoint-run` — ANY tool whose "full" response is rich enough to need heavy generic
trimming (no custom `shape.trimmed`/`shape.standard` declared) and whose write/launch outcome
lives in non-canonical field names is exposed to the same failure: the more information a reply
needs to trim away, the more likely its own trim-bookkeeping is to eat the reply itself.

If you own a tool whose success/failure the caller cannot re-derive by retrying (a launch, a
kill, a claim, anything with real side effects) and it can return a large/nested payload, prefer
declaring an explicit `shape.trimmed` that puts the outcome fields first — don't rely solely on
the generic projector's fallback, even after this fix. The fallback is now a safety net that
degrades gracefully to *identity only*, not a substitute for a tool-authored shaper that knows
which fields actually matter.

## Where

- `libs/generic/tooldef/src/payload-tier.ts` — `projectBoundedPayload`'s last-line defense,
  `IDENTITY_FIELDS`.
- Regression test: `libs/generic/tooldef/src/payload-tier.test.ts` (search
  `EI-21058972492075433`) — models `release:checkpoint-run`'s actual launch-receipt shape.
